title: How to Make Good Habits Inevitable and Bad Habits Impossible
coreMove: Lock a future choice in place today by building a commitment device that removes the option to defect when willpower is lowest.

exampleSpecs.domain: a pediatric night-shift nurse who keeps scrolling TikTok until 4am on her days off and wrecking her sleep cycle
exampleSpecs.audience: a shift worker whose schedule already fights them
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she shows up to a 12-hour shift with the cognition of a drunk driver
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she physically hands her phone to her roommate at 10pm with a written note saying 'do not return until 7am no matter what I say', and the doc shows the moment she would have caved if the option were still hers

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school orchestra teacher trying to stop checking work email on weekends
exampleSpecs.audience: a salaried professional with no enforced boundaries
exampleSpecs.stakes: a marriage that is quietly running on fumes because Saturday is never actually Saturday
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before: he white-knuckles a 'no email Saturday' rule and fails by 10am; after: he deletes the mail app from his phone every Friday at 5pm and the friction is enough that Saturday survives

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance illustrator who keeps eating an entire sleeve of cookies while drawing at her kitchen table
exampleSpecs.audience: someone who works from home with the pantry six feet away
exampleSpecs.stakes: a creeping pre-diabetic A1C her doctor flagged in March
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she narrates the small physical act of taping the pantry shut with painter's tape every morning, and the moment at 3pm when she stands in front of it, considers peeling the tape, and walks away because peeling tape feels stupid in a way that opening a cupboard does not

exampleSpecs.domain: a city council aide trying to write a book proposal in the 5am hour before work
exampleSpecs.audience: someone with one fragile pocket of time and no slack
exampleSpecs.stakes: a manuscript that has been 'almost started' for three years
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reader is asked what single commitment device would make tomorrow's 5am writing inevitable; the reveal shows the aide pre-paying a Saturday writing coach $400/week who only gets paid if he sends pages by Friday — a stake he cannot quietly renegotiate with himself

exampleSpecs.domain: a recovering gambler who still drives past the off-track betting parlor on his commute home
exampleSpecs.audience: someone for whom one slip costs more than a slip should
exampleSpecs.stakes: eighteen months of recovery and a daughter who just started trusting him again
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reader is asked to design two commitment devices, one that costs nothing and one that costs real money, that would make the next slip mechanically harder; the doc must compare which one would survive a bad Tuesday and why

exampleSpecs.domain: a partner at a small law firm who promises every January to leave the office by 6pm and never does
exampleSpecs.audience: a senior professional whose calendar is the problem
exampleSpecs.stakes: a back that has begun to spasm and a teenager who has stopped asking about dinner
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a conversation with her office manager in which she asks him to lock her office at 6:01pm and refuse to reopen it; the dialogue lands on the discomfort of giving someone else the authority she will not exercise on herself, and why that transfer is the whole mechanism
